lines: Nobody tells you why good surfers paddle out where no waves break.
That calm strip is a rip, pulling the water back out to sea.
For them it's a free ride to the lineup. Two moves.
One. From the sand, find the gap where the waves don't break.
Two. Paddle out in it, then slide sideways to the peak.
You get there with fresh arms.
New to surfing? Stay out of rips. Caught in one? Paddle parallel to the beach.
Save it for the next paddle-out that takes forever.
Bigger swell, stronger rip. Check the wave height in Surf Tribe first.
Tomorrow, why big boards aren't just for beginners.
